Free the APIC access page memslot if any vCPU enables x2APIC and SVM's
AVIC is enabled to prevent accesses to the virtual APIC on vCPUs with
x2APIC enabled.  On AMD
column2: if its ""hybrid"" mode is enabled (AVIC is enabled

column1: when x2APIC is enabled even without x2AVIC support)
access page memslot results in the guest being able to access the virtual
APIC page as x2APIC is fully emulated by KVM.  I.e. hardware isn't aware
that the guest is operating in x2APIC mode.
Exempt nested SVM's update of APICv state from the new logic as x2APIC
can't be toggled on VM-Exit.  In practice
should be harmless precisely because it should be a glorified nop
play it safe to avoid latent bugs
column2: e.g. with dropping the vCPU's SRCU

column1: lock.
Intel doesn't suffer from the same issue as APICv has fully independent
VMCS controls for xAPIC vs. x2APIC virtualization.  Technically
should provide bus error semantics and not memory semantics for the APIC
page when x2APIC is enabled
column2: but KVM already provides memory semantics in

column1: other scenarios
column2: e.g. if APICv/AVIC is enabled and the APIC is hardware

column1: disabled (via APIC_BASE MSR).
Note
column2: checking apic_access_memslot_enabled without taking locks relies

column1: it being set during vCPU creation (before kvm_vcpu_reset()).  vCPUs can
race to set the inhibit and delete the memslot
positives
column2: but can't get false negatives as apic_access_memslot_enabled

column1: can't be toggled ""on"" once any vCPU reaches KVM_RUN.

comment
column2: i.e. to state that KVM _does_ support the hybrid mode.  Move

Opportunistically update the apicv_update_lock comment
actually used to protect apic_access_memslot_enabled (which is protected
by slots_lock).
